\begin{chapstatus}{The thread of this chapter}
You now own the whole cycle: write a source file, translate it, send the cartridge to a host, stop it in the debugger. Next: writing the source file yourself.
\par\medskip\textbf{Exit ticket} (two to four minutes, alone, on paper):
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=2em]
\item Put these four in order and say in one line what each does: the cartridge, the source file, the runtime of a host, the assembler.
\item In a new terminal you type python3 -m prg32 doctor and read: idf.py: command not found. What does the message tell you, and what do you do first?
\end{enumerate}
\end{chapstatus}
